name: Standard Scramble

waypoints.name: Thirtymile Trailhead
waypoints.note: Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issue Pasayten Wilderness permit are required at the trailhead kiosk; no potable water on site.
waypoints.directions: Park at the Thirtymile Trailhead, at the end of West Chewuch Road, about 29 miles north of Winthrop. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issue Pasayten Wilderness permit, available at the trailhead kiosk, are both required, and there is no potable water on site. The road in and the high country beyond often don't fully clear of snow until late June or early July, so plan an early-season trip accordingly.

waypoints.name: Campsite below Tungsten Creek ford
waypoints.note: Established campsite on the Chewuch River roughly a quarter-mile before the Tungsten Creek ford — the last sheltered camp before the crossing.
waypoints.directions: Follow Chewuch River Trail #510 north from the trailhead, staying near the river. Chewuch Falls is a landmark about 2.5 miles in; farther on the trail crosses the 2001 burn, where standing snags can fall in wind. Continue about 8.5 miles in all to the established camp on the river roughly a quarter mile before the Tungsten Creek ford.

waypoints.name: Tungsten Creek ford
waypoints.note: Unbridged, knee-deep, fast-flowing ford of Tungsten Creek; a genuine hazard during snowmelt or after rain, best crossed early in the day.
waypoints.directions: Continue about a quarter mile up the trail to the unbridged ford of Tungsten Creek. It runs knee-deep and fast in snowmelt or after rain, so cross early in the day.

waypoints.name: Tungsten Creek Trail #534 junction
waypoints.note: Leave the Chewuch Trail #510 here onto Tungsten Creek Trail #534, climbing away from the river through young lodgepole regrowth from the 2001 burn.
waypoints.directions: Just beyond the ford, reach the signed junction where Tungsten Creek Trail #534 leaves the Chewuch River Trail, and take the Tungsten Creek Trail.

waypoints.name: Tungsten Mine Camp / Boundary Trail #533 junction
waypoints.note: Site of the defunct early-1900s tungsten mine — two collapsed buildings and brick mill remnants remain; meets Boundary Trail #533 here.
waypoints.directions: Tungsten Creek Trail #534 climbs about 6.2 miles and 2,100 ft, steeply at first through trees with a few switchbacks, then along a sidehill through meadows, crossing Cinch Creek. The creek the trail follows on its last stretch is the final dependable water. The trail ends at its junction with Boundary Trail #533 at the old mine camp, with ruins and iron pipe on the slope.

waypoints.name: Boundary Trail bend toward Apex Pass
waypoints.note: Boundary Trail bends south toward Apex Pass here; leave the trail and head off-trail north/northeast up Wolframite's broad, gentle west slopes (Class 2).

waypoints.name: Wolframite Mountain summit
waypoints.note: True summit on open talus/tundra; broad views over the Pasayten Wilderness backcountry and Canadian border peaks.

approach: Park at the Thirtymile Trailhead (~3,400 ft) at the end of West Chewuch Road, about 29 miles north of Winthrop. From there follow the Chewuch River Trail #510 north, staying close to the Chewuch River; Chewuch Falls is a good landmark around 2.5 miles in. Around mile 8 to 8.8 the trail crosses a 2001 burn area — standing dead snags are common here and more prone to falling in wind, so be alert in storms. At roughly 8-8.8 miles (~4,700 ft) reach the signed junction with Tungsten Creek Trail #534 and turn right (northeast). Follow Tungsten Creek Trail #534 for 6.2 miles, gaining about 2,100 ft, passing within earshot of Big Horn and Horseshoe Creeks and crossing Cinch Creek; Tungsten Creek itself, which the trail follows for its final stretch, is the last dependable water before the high country (in dry years, e.g. a September 2017 trip, sources beyond here were reported as dry streambeds and stagnant pools, so tank up). This trail ends at its junction with the Boundary Trail #533 at the historic Tungsten Mine Camp (~6,750 ft) — old mine structures, iron pipe, and building ruins from the 1908-1920s tungsten operation are visible on the south side of Wolframite Mountain. This point is roughly 14-15 miles in, effectively a full day's hike, and most parties camp near here rather than pushing to the summit and back in one day. From the mine camp junction, follow the Boundary Trail #533 west/south for about 1 mile to the point where the trail bends south toward Apex Pass. Leave the trail here and ascend off-trail, heading northeast up Wolframite's broad, gentle west slopes to the 8,136-8,137 ft summit; done on this line the terrain is a straightforward Class 2 talus/heather slope, though other lines or variations can involve short sections of low Class 3. This is the safest and most recommended line up the peak. Total one-way distance from the trailhead is roughly 16-17 miles with about 4,700 ft of cumulative gain, consistent with the ~34-mile (54.72 km) round trip — treat this as a backpack with a high camp near Tungsten Mine or the Boundary Trail, not a single-day car-to-car scramble.

pitch_detail.notes: 12-21 miles one-way (trailhead-dependent) via Cathedral Driveway/Chewuch/Tungsten Creek Trails or the Boundary Trail from Iron Gate, to Tungsten Mine Camp.
~1 mile west/northwest on Boundary Trail #533 from the Tungsten Mine Camp junction to where the trail bends south.
Off-trail ascent northeast up the gentle west-facing slope to the summit; steeper/looser variations exist on other aspects.
